## Full current page content [food-safety]

# Food Safety

Preventing foodborne illness through proper handling, storage, and preparation.

## Temperature Danger Zone

Bacteria multiply rapidly between 4 °C and 60 °C. Perishable food should not remain in this range for more than two hours (one hour above 32 °C ambient).


> [!warning] Contradiction — CD-001 · open
> **A** — 2026-08-12 · `src/seed-corpus` — Bacteria multiply rapidly in the temperature range of 4 °C to 60 °C.
> **B** — 2026-08-12 · `src/8271c9cd-food-safety-update` — Bacteria multiply rapidly in the temperature range of 5 °C to 63 °C.
> The two claims assign different numeric boundaries to the same bacterial growth range, and the source never states that the previously accepted figures were revised to the new ones.

> [!warning] Contradiction — CD-002 · open
> **A** — 2026-08-12 · `src/seed-corpus` — Perishable food should not remain in the temperature range of 4 °C to 60 °C for more than two hours.
> **B** — 2026-08-12 · `src/8271c9cd-food-safety-update` — Food held in the temperature range of 5 °C to 63 °C for more than two hours should be discarded.
> Both state a two-hour limit but over incompatible temperature ranges, with no explicit statement in the source that the range was changed.
## Cross-Contamination

Raw meat, poultry, and seafood must be stored below ready-to-eat foods. Separate cutting boards and utensils prevent transfer of pathogens like Salmonella and Campylobacter.


Updated 2024 guidance states the danger zone as 5 °C to 63 °C, and advises that food held in this range for more than two hours be discarded. The differing figures (4–60 °C vs. 5–63 °C) reflect different national standards rather than a change in the underlying microbiology; the narrower range is the more conservative in practice.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

Refrigerators should maintain temperatures below 5 °C at all times, not merely on average. Verify with an appliance thermometer rather than relying on the dial setting, and allow for temperature rise when the door is opened frequently or the unit is overpacked.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

Cooking to a sufficient internal temperature is the primary control for pathogens that handling and storage practices cannot eliminate.

All poultry products — including chicken, turkey, and duck — should reach an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving. This figure was revised downward from a previous recommendation of 82 °C in 2024, on the basis of updated pathogen destruction research; the earlier figure is superseded rather than merely an alternative standard.

*(Source: examples/poultry-temperature-revision.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

# Sauerkraut Fermentation

Basic sauerkraut fermentation takes 14 days at room temperature. The cabbage should be submerged in its own brine throughout the process to prevent mould growth.
